title: Dynamical locality and covariance: What makes a physical theory the same in all spacetimes?
relevance: Source of Loc and Loc_0. Its multi-diamond objects make the germ theorem near-immediate. Its Sec. 4.3 is a prior use of scalar curvature to build order-valued functors.
limits: Selected pages only. Secs. 3.3-3.4, 5-7 and most of the appendices not read.
locator: Sec. 2.1 with Prop. 2.1 (objects, finitely many components); Sec. 2.2 (Loc, Loc_0, morphisms, causal disjointness of components, O(M)); Def. 2.5 (diamonds, multi-diamonds); Prop. 2.6 (chains of morphisms); Def. 4.1 (SPASs); Sec. 4.3 eq. (4.5) (scalar-curvature threshold functor)
assumptions: Globally hyperbolic spacetimes of fixed dimension; smooth, paracompact, orientable, finitely many components.
conclusion: Authors' definitions and results as located. The full class of locally covariant theories fails SPASs; dynamically local theories satisfy it.
proof_status: Definitions and Sec. 4.3 construction read; proofs of Props 2.2, 2.4 and Lemmas A.5-A.6 read; main theorems of Secs. 5-6 not read.
open_questions: Whether a statement equivalent to the no-spacelike-scale proposition appears in Secs. 3-6 or in later work on Einstein causality.
